# Onto Innovation: dated operating valuation and conditional claims bridge, v2

Research cutoff: 18 October 2026. Capital and discount origin: 30 June 2026. Currency: USD; financial amounts in millions unless stated otherwise.

## Review decision

ONTO is eligible for the requested U.S. universe: its [official Robinhood U.S. page](https://robinhood.com/us/en/stocks/ONTO/) offers stock purchase and sale, and its [SEC filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/704532/000119312526338401/onto-20260630.htm) identifies NYSE common stock. This verifies public product availability, not this user's account permissions.

The v1 operating arithmetic received a qualified independent pass. Version2 applies its factual and disclosure corrections and awaits reviewer closure. Exact current equity value, a current price target, and an accepted per-share valuation remain blocked. The June capped-call fair value, gross legacy award claims, current ESPP rights, and a complete opening tax/capital-payable ledger are not separately disclosed in the reviewed material. Conditional calculations are shown to make the missing claims visible, not to pretend they have been measured. No app files were edited or published.

## Business and evidence

Onto supplies optical metrology, defect inspection, advanced-packaging lithography, analytical software, parts and service. The annual financial statements have one reportable segment. Management's advanced-node and packaging market categories are different from the filing's product-revenue categories.

H1 2026 revenue was $635.1m, with systems/software at 85.2%, parts 8.7%, and service 6.1%. Four customers represented 57.3% of sales; five customers represented 64.3% of receivables. Taiwan and South Korea accounted for 56.3% of shipments. Shipping geography is not ultimate end-use geography. Semilab contributed $46.1m of H1 sales and a $9m operating loss. Subtracting that contribution reduces reported H1 sales growth from 22.1% to 13.2%; this arithmetic is not a fully adjusted organic-growth measure. [Q2 filing, Notes 2 and 13 and MD&A](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/704532/000119312526338401/onto-20260630.htm)

The January CEO fireside deck estimated that AI-related applications generated 61% of 2025 revenue. It described additional applications for Dragonfly inspection, GAA metrology and silicon photonics, expected tariff/local-manufacturing benefits, and targeted $120m of 2026 Semilab sales. These are management definitions and forecasts. No audio was consumed. [January presentation](https://s24.q4cdn.com/480160064/files/doc_presentations/2026/Jan/13/Onto-Innovation-Investor-Update_January-2026.pdf)

The August call transcript, hosted by a third party, describes second-half revenue growth of at least 25%, Q4 above Q3, roughly $1.1bn backlog, and order delivery extending into 2027. Management attributed margin improvement to the extended factories and expected a rising Dragonfly G5 mix. The transcript contains visible transcription errors and is corroborative evidence, not an independently verified customer-order book. No full transcript is included in the public-safe package. [Management call transcription](https://www.earningswhispers.com/transcript/ONTO/Q22026)

Acquisition amortization, restructuring, and transaction costs explain much of the gap between GAAP and adjusted margins. Ordinary SBC remains inside the company's adjusted operating result. ## Ten-year history and comparability

The machine-readable history contains fiscal 2016–2025 revenue, gross profit, EBIT, pretax profit, taxes, net income, cash flow, physical capex/depreciation, acquired amortization, SBC, R&D and selected balance-sheet components, each with filing/tag/period provenance.

Revenue / GAAP EBIT, in millions:

- 2016: 232.780 / 52.348
- 2017: 255.098 / 59.288
- 2018: 273.784 / 51.084
- 2019: 305.896 / −5.043
- 2020: 556.496 / 26.677
- 2021: 788.899 / 156.407
- 2022: 1,005.183 / 236.714
- 2023: 815.868 / 116.078
- 2024: 987.321 / 187.103
- 2025: 1,005.263 / 132.927

2016–2018 are Rudolph, the accounting predecessor. They are not standalone Nanometrics. The reverse acquisition took effect in October 2019, so 2019 includes only the post-merger Nanometrics period; disclosed combined pro-forma 2019 sales were $525.455m. The 0.8042 exchange ratio affects predecessor share comparability. Earlier Rudolph shares and later merger-restated comparatives are explicitly labelled; they are not used as a continuous current denominator. Patent-litigation income of $14.643m and $13m also inflated 2016 and 2017 EBIT. [2019 annual report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/704532/000156459020006357/onto-10k_20191231.htm)

FY2020 was shortened to361inclusive days, January1–December26, as fiscal-calendar policy changed. 2021 and 2025 were53-week fiscal years. A filing-derived FY2025-minus-H12025-plus-H12026 anchor produces $1,120.137m sales, but spans roughly 367 days because of fiscal-calendar transitions. It is a rolling reported-period approximation, not an exact normalized 365-day run rate. Semilab contributed only $8.6m in 2025. [2025 annual](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/704532/000119312526066937/onto-20260103.htm)

Later comparative XBRL observations contained erroneous signs/period contexts for 2019–2021. Those years are locked to the original annual statements, rather than blindly selecting the latest tag. The positive 2020 and 2021 operating profits reconcile to the source statements. [2020 annual](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/704532/000156459021006843/onto-10k_20201226.htm), [2021 annual](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/704532/000156459022006948/onto-10k_20220101.htm)

Historical invested-capital diagnostics are deliberately labelled narrow proxies: receivables plus inventory less AP, accruals and current deferred revenue, plus physical assets and a 3% operating-cash assumption. They exclude several unallocated assets and liabilities. Missing predecessor accrual data stays blank. These are not audited comprehensive economic ROICs.

## Explicit operating model

The model has ten annual cash-flow periods beginning July 2026. The first base year combines Q3 guidance midpoint $390m, analyst Q4 sales $420m, and analyst H1 2027 sales $850m. Later calendar-year assumptions use an equal-half-year allocation. There is no invented actual cash/share roll-forward.

Base first-five-year sales are $1,660m, $1,825m, $2,067m, $2,264m and $2,444m. Economic operating margins are 30%, 31%, 31.5%, 31% and 30.5%, fading to 28%. Downcycle margins and sales explicitly weaken after the near-term demand burst; upside requires sustained product adoption and pricing. These are analyst scenarios, not company guidance.

Growth is funded. Early base reinvestment is the larger of incremental sales divided by 1.4, or a cash-funding floor: 3% physical cash capex less 1.8% physical depreciation, plus 40% of positive incremental revenue for operating working capital and 3% for operating cash. No working-capital release is credited when sales fall. Additional investment above the floor is explicitly identified. This is an aggregate capacity/working-capital model, not a claim that every balance-sheet line has been independently projected.

The base 1.4 sales-to-capital assumption is more demanding than recent narrow historical proxies around 1.4–1.9. Outsourced factories support modest physical capex, but inventory and receivables remain substantial. Unmeasured opening capital payables are a bridge limitation; future cash capex is not financed by an assumed free payable increase.

From year six, reinvestment converges to growth/terminal ROIC. Base terminal growth is 3%, ROIC 18%, economic operating margin 28% and tax 21%. Downcycle uses 2.5% growth/12% ROIC/23% margin; upside uses 3.5%/22%/31%. Every last explicit year exactly meets its terminal reinvestment ratio and still covers the physical/NWC/cash floor. These ROIC inputs are assumed sustainable returns used to fund incremental terminal growth, not measured company-wide returns on a complete economic capital rollforward. Taxes fade from 15% to 21%; transient stock-compensation benefits and acquisition tax effects are not perpetuated.

## Compensation without double counting

Fresh 2025 grants were 315k RSUs at $102.59 grant-date value and 49k target PRSUs at $140.94 fair value, together $39.222m or 3.90% of sales before ESPP. This exceeds the 2.75% recognized SBC ratio. The combined 400k grants table includes extra shares on old performance awards and is not a clean measure of new compensation. New grants cost 4.2% of forecast revenue initially, fading to 3.5%, inside economic margins. Future grants are not also charged through future dilution. [Annual, Note 11](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/704532/000119312526066937/onto-20260103.htm)

June unrecognized legacy expense was $59.4m over a two-year weighted period. A $29.7m/$29.7m display schedule is deducted and identically reversed before NOPAT; timing cannot create value. Old awards are charged once through conditional gross full-value-equivalent shares. January's 402k service units and 82k target PRSUs do not establish June units. Conditional 0.4m/0.75m/1.2m legacy units and $0m/$3m/$6m ESPP claims are stress assumptions, not reported counts or confidence bounds. The publication gate stays closed. [Q2, Note 10](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/704532/000119312526338401/onto-20260630.htm)

## Dated claims bridge

June cash and marketable securities total $1,882.150m. The operating reserve is $33.604m. A privately held investment is carried at $8m, with $0–8m recovery tested. Separately known unpaid financing costs and repurchase excise tax total $4.669m. The $1.5bn zero-coupon convertible has $1,471.731m carrying value but a disclosed June Level-2 fair value of $1,982.250m. [Q2, Notes 3 and 7 and cash-flow supplement](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/704532/000119312526338401/onto-20260630.htm)

The conditional bridge subtracts the entire convertible fair-value claim. It does not also subtract face value or add full conversion shares. This market-measured claim is held fixed across operating scenarios, so it is not a complete intrinsic repricing of the security.

The notes require cash settlement up to principal. The capped calls cover the original 3.9288m underlying shares, with $381.796 strike and $509.06 cap. The contract uses 30-day averaging and default net-share settlement, with alternative cash/combination methods following the note election. It excludes specified voluntary/make-whole conversion adjustments. Coverage is therefore not perfect. [Issuance](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/704532/000119312526234610/d17904d8k.htm), [confirmation](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/704532/000119312526234610/d17904dex101.htm)

No current capped-call fair value is disclosed. $0, the historical $88.95m premium, and an approximately $500m unadjusted nominal payoff-cap stress are displayed; none is claimed as measured June fair value. The last figure is conditional on unchanged terms, not a universal corporate-event bound. No separate dilution-offset credit is added.

The [August 10 closing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/704532/000119312526341337/d125405d8k.htm) bought 27% of Rigaku for approximately $720m. The June-origin bridge includes both the future $720m cash payment and a same-date minority-asset valuation assumption, discounted over 41 days. At cost they offset. At 70% recovery, value falls by approximately $214.85m. Rigaku sales are not consolidated in the operating forecast. The model never calls June cash October cash.

Current residual tax, capital-payable and other nonoperating claims are not completely mapped. A conditional $15m allowance is anchored to January income taxes payable plus recorded noncurrent uncertain-tax liabilities of $14.293m, with $0–30m tested. This is not an observed June amount or a rigorous bound. Gross uncertain-tax benefits must not be added to the recorded liability again. Deferred tax book balances and the capped-call tax asset are not independently credited at face value. Rent remains an operating cost, with no second deduction of operating-lease debt.

## Rates, results and limits

The October 16 Treasury ten-year rate is 5.09%. The October 1 Damodaran implied ERP is 4.20%, with 0.22% U.S. default spread: the internally consistent adjusted inputs are 4.87% risk-free and 4.42% ERP. The January equipment-sector cash-corrected unlevered beta is 1.39. A 5% assumed permanent debt weight, 150bp credit spread, and 21% tax produce 10.966% initial WACC, fading to 9.506% using terminal equity beta 1.1. These maturity/leverage inputs are judgments; the convertible's zero coupon is not its cost of capital. [Treasury](https://home.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/TextView?type=daily_treasury_yield_curve&field_tdr_date_value=2026&field_tdr_date_value_month=202610), [ERP](https://pages.stern.nyu.edu/~adamodar/New_Home_Page/home.htm), [sector beta](https://pages.stern.nyu.edu/~adamodar/New_Home_Page/datafile/Betas.html)

Calculated June-origin operating enterprise values:

- Downcycle: $2,643m
- Base: $5,867m
- Upside: $10,232m

For illustration only, the explicitly unmeasured middle bridge inputs yield $47.57/$116.66/$204.33 per share. These are conditional demonstrations, not accepted price targets. Exact current equity/per-share fields remain null. No current-price upside, scenario probability, or trade recommendation is produced.

The full annual schedules, WACC/margin/new-grant stresses and one-at-a-time claim sensitivities accompany the report. Review priorities are claims measurement, revenue timing, recurring restructuring economics, capital intensity and terminal durability. The independent v1 review reproduced operating arithmetic and required the factual/disclosure amendments below. v2 amendments still require reviewer closure; that review does not accept current equity claims.

## Version2 audit corrections and remaining operating/claims questions
Original v1 and its independent audit remain preserved. Base/down/up operating EVs are unchanged. No exact current equity or per-share gate is reopened.

- Predecessor R&D: FY2016 originally classified R&D44.964 is retained; comparable merger-reclassified R&D35.797 is added. FY2015 likewise retains41.233 and adds32.689. Applications engineering moved to sales/marketing; EBIT does not change. Companion history/CSV explicitly distinguish both classifications. [2019 selected financial data, footnote2](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/704532/000156459020006357/onto-10k_20191231.htm)
- The19.3 capped-call DTA arose in May2026 and was reported in June, rather than existing at the January annual date. It is now separately dated and still receives no automatic face-value tax credit. [Q2 Note7](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/704532/000119312526338401/onto-20260630.htm)
- June FX forwards have a1.284 fair-value asset on79.847 notional, outside cash/marketables. Their underlying exposure, tax and settlement need mapping before choosing an equity credit versus operating cash-flow treatment. The asset is separately identified and unresolved; the notional is never treated as value. [Q2 Notes3and5](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/704532/000119312526338401/onto-20260630.htm)
- The June18 headquarters lease replaces the old Wilmington office, begins approximately2027 and has a roughly13-year term,3% annual increases, early abatements and phased commencement. Initial full-area annual rent is about2.719 before abatements, with total undiscounted payments36.4. It was unrecognized at June. Aggregate margins include rent, but the old/new occupancy schedule is unresolved. Do not deduct36.4 as debt in addition to rent. [Q2 Note8](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/704532/000119312526338401/onto-20260630.htm)
- A separate20bp operating-margin cost-headroom stress, with funded reinvestment preserved, reduces base EV by46.389 to5820.833. Its first-year added cost3.32 exceeds the disclosed initial full-area rent; it ignores replacement savings/abatements and continues beyond the lease term. This is an intentionally demanding sensitivity, not an estimate of actual incremental lease cost.
- January zero deferred-compensation balance cannot establish June zero after2026 deferrals begin. Residual tax/capital claims and old awards remain unknown.
- Terminal returns are incremental growth-funding assumptions. The paired Rigaku cash/asset discount is illustrative: a future risky minority stake needs its own risk-consistent value, rights/FX/liquidity analysis, and cannot automatically be valued at purchase cost.
- Rate observations use October1 ERP and October16 Treasury, not synchronized daily inputs. Supplemental source inventory hashes all retained files, records actual known retrieval dates and leaves missing dates unknown.
